## Getting Started

### Installing and Loading Packages

```{r, eval=F}
#install a package (only once per computer)
install.packages("PACKAGE_NAME")

#load a package (every time you start R)
library(PACKAGE_NAME)
```

### Reading In Data

```{r, eval=F}
#read a spatial file (.geojson, .shp, .gpkg) or a Google Drive download link
DATA <- st_read("FILE_PATH_OR_URL")

#read a csv file
DATA <- read_csv("FILE_PATH_OR_URL")

#read a raster file (.tif) (requires terra package)
RASTER <- rast("FILE_PATH_OR_URL")

#load objects saved in an .RData file
load("FILE_NAME.RData")
```

### Looking at Data

```{r, eval=F}
#look at the columns and their types
glimpse(DATA)

#open the data in a spreadsheet view
View(DATA)

#see the first 6 rows
head(DATA)

#number of rows
nrow(DATA)

#count how many rows have each value of a column
table(DATA$VARIABLE)
```

## Basic Data Manipulation

### Creating Objects

Creating an object allows you to store the output of a command in the environment. This means you can reuse the result later by referencing the object name, instead of rerunning the command every time.

```{r, eval=F}

## When this command runs, it will show up in the environment
chart <- ggplot(DATASET_OBJECT, aes(y = VARIABLE_OF_INTEREST)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "lightgrey")

##now I can "call" the object
chart

```

### Filtering Data

To create our analytical dataset we often need to subset a larger dataset. Filtering allows us to simplify. We always want to save filtered data as objects so that we can reference them in other commands.

```{r, eval=F}
#to select certain columns
columns <- DATASET |> select(COLUMN1, COLUMN2, COLUMN3)

### IF VALUES ARE STRING (NON-NUMERIC) THEY MUST BE IN ""

#to filter by values in a certain column
values <- DATASET |> filter(COLUMN == VALUE)

# to filter by multiple conditions.
#and
values <- DATASET |> filter(COLUMN == VALUE & COLUMN2 == VALUE2)

#or
values <- DATASET |> filter(COLUMN == VALUE | COLUMN2 == VALUE2)

#in
values <- DATASET |> filter(COLUMN %in% c(VALUE1, VALUE2, VALUE3))

#numeric operator
values <- DATASET |> filter(COLUMN < 2000)

```

### Making New Columns

```{r, eval=F}
#creating new columns
dataset <- DATASET |> mutate(NEWCOLUMN = COMMAND, NEWCOLUMN2 = COMMAND)

#a column that is 1 when a condition is true and 0 when it is false
dataset <- DATASET |> mutate(NEWCOLUMN = ifelse(VARIABLE > VALUE, 1, 0))

#recode 1 and 0 into labels
dataset <- DATASET |> mutate(NEWCOLUMN = ifelse(VARIABLE == 1, "LABEL_IF_1", "LABEL_IF_0"))

#the difference between two columns
dataset <- DATASET |> mutate(diff = VARIABLE2 - VARIABLE1)
```

### Renaming Columns

```{r, eval=F}
#renaming columns
clean_data <- DATASET |> rename(
  new_name1 = old_name1,
  new_name2 = old_name2
)

```

### Removing Missing Values and Duplicates

```{r, eval=F}
#drop rows with a missing value in any of the listed columns
complete <- DATA |> drop_na(VARIABLE1, VARIABLE2)

#how many rows were dropped
nrow(DATA) - nrow(complete)

#drop rows that are exact copies of another row
DATA <- DATA |> distinct()

#drop points that share exact coordinates with an earlier point
DATA <- DATA |> filter(!duplicated(st_coordinates(DATA)))
```

### Grouping and Summarizing Data

```{r, eval=F}

summary_data <- DATASET |>
  group_by(CATEGORY_COLUMN) |>
  summarize(
    mean_value = mean(NUMERIC_COLUMN, na.rm = TRUE),
    count = n()
  )
```

### Sorting and Picking Rows

```{r, eval=F}
#sort from smallest to largest (use desc(VARIABLE) for largest to smallest)
sorted <- DATA |> arrange(VARIABLE)

#keep the first N rows
first_rows <- DATA |> slice_head(n = N)

#keep the N rows with the largest values of a variable
top_rows <- DATA |> slice_max(VARIABLE, n = N)

#pull one column out as a vector
values <- DATA |> pull(VARIABLE)

#keep only unique rows (or unique values of a column)
unique_rows <- DATA |> distinct(VARIABLE)

#count the number of unique values
DATA |> summarize(n_unique = n_distinct(VARIABLE))
```

### Counts and Proportions

```{r, eval=F}
#number of rows where a condition is true
sum(DATA$VARIABLE > VALUE)

#share of rows where a condition is true
mean(DATA$VARIABLE > VALUE)

#two-way table of counts
counts <- table(DATA$VARIABLE1, DATA$VARIABLE2)

#turn the counts into proportions within each row
prop.table(counts, margin = 1)
```

### Making Random Results Repeatable

```{r, eval=F}
#run this right before any command that uses random numbers (sample, simulations, permutation tests)
set.seed(391)
```

### Creating a Spatial Object

```{r, eval = F}
#assumes a nonspatial object with a longitude and latitude field (longitude goes first)
DATA_sf <- DATA |> st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326)

#drop the geometry to get a regular table
DATA_table <- DATA_sf |> st_drop_geometry()

#make a table of the x and y coordinates and one variable
DATA_df <- data.frame(x = st_coordinates(DATA_sf)[, 1],
                      y = st_coordinates(DATA_sf)[, 2],
                      value = DATA_sf$VARIABLE)
```

### Projecting and Other Spatial Operations

```{r, eval=F}
#reproject to a new coordinate reference system
#2264 = NC State Plane in feet, 32119 = NC State Plane in meters
DATA_projected <- st_transform(DATA, crs = EPSG_CODE)

#find the center point of each polygon
centroids <- st_centroid(DATA)

#draw a buffer around features (distance is in the units of the CRS)
buffered <- st_buffer(DATA, dist = DISTANCE)

#distance between every feature in two datasets (in the units of the CRS)
distances <- st_distance(DATA1, DATA2)

#keep only the features of DATA1 that fall inside DATA2
inside <- DATA1 |> st_filter(DATA2)

#merge many polygons (for example counties) into one outline
outline <- st_union(DATA)

#just the geometry, without the attribute columns
st_geometry(DATA)
```

## Descriptive Statistics

### Descriptive Statistics Tables

```{r, eval=F}
#requires e1071 package
#requires gt package
## descriptive statistics for quantitative data
DATASET_OBJECT |> #whatever the object is named
  st_drop_geometry() |> #gets rid of geometry column
  select(VARIABLE_OF_INTEREST) |> #field name of variable of interest
  summarise(                  #summarizes variable of interest. You can add/remove
    n = n(),
    num_na = sum(is.na(VARIABLE_OF_INTEREST)),
    mean = mean(VARIABLE_OF_INTEREST, na.rm = TRUE),
    median = median(VARIABLE_OF_INTEREST, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = sd(VARIABLE_OF_INTEREST, na.rm = TRUE),
    variance = var(VARIABLE_OF_INTEREST, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_dev = mean(abs(VARIABLE_OF_INTEREST - mean(VARIABLE_OF_INTEREST, na.rm = TRUE)), na.rm = TRUE),
    cv = sd / mean,
    min = min(VARIABLE_OF_INTEREST, na.rm = TRUE),
    max = max(VARIABLE_OF_INTEREST, na.rm = TRUE),
    skewness = skewness(VARIABLE_OF_INTEREST, na.rm = TRUE),
    kurtosis = kurtosis(VARIABLE_OF_INTEREST, na.rm = TRUE) #excess kurtosis, so a normal distribution is 0
  ) |>
  #this starts the table formatting.
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "Statistic", values_to = "Value") |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(
    title = "TITLE" ##Add your title here
  ) |>
  fmt_number(
    columns = Value,
    decimals = 2 ##You can change number of decimals
  )

## Descriptive statistics table for categorical data
DATASET_OBJECT |> #whatever the object is named
  st_drop_geometry() |> #gets rid of geometry column
  group_by(CATEGORICAL_VARIABLE) |> #variable that you want to summarize
  summarise(n = n())  |> #calculates the count
  gt() #formats into a table

```

### Histogram

```{r, eval=F}
#requires ggplot2 package
## Create a basic histogram.
## You will likely need to modify the binwidth command
ggplot(DATASET_OBJECT, aes(x = VARIABLE_OF_INTEREST)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 1, fill = "lightgrey", color = "black", alpha = 0.7) +
  labs(
    title = "TITLE",
    x = "X-AXIS LABEL",
    y = "Y-AXIS LABEL"
  )

```

### Boxplot

```{r, eval = F}
#requires ggplot2 package
# create basic boxplot
ggplot(DATASET_OBJECT, aes(y = VARIABLE_OF_INTEREST)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "lightgrey") +
  labs(
    title = "TITLE",
    y = "Y-AXIS LABEL"
  )

```

### Violin Plot

```{r,  eval = F}
#requires ggplot2 package
##you will likely need to modify the bw
ggplot(DATASET_OBJECT, aes(x = 1, y = VARIABLE_OF_INTEREST)) +
  geom_violin(fill = "lightgrey", bw = 1.2)  + geom_boxplot(width=0.1) +
  labs(
    title = "TITLE",
    y = "Y AXIS LABEL"
  ) + theme(axis.title.x=element_blank(),
        axis.text.x=element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.x=element_blank())

```

### Bar Chart

```{r, eval = F}
#requires ggplot2 package
##YOU NEED TO FIRST GROUP THE DATA
grouped_data <- DATASET_OBJECT |> st_drop_geometry() |>
  group_by(VARIABLE_OF_INTEREST) |>
  summarise(Count = n())

#this plots the bar plot (note that the coord_flip switches the axis which is optional)
ggplot(grouped_data, aes(x = VARIABLE_OF_INTEREST, y = Count)) +
  geom_col() + coord_flip() + labs(
    x = "X_AXIS_LABEL",
    y = "Y_AXIS_LABEL"
  )

```

### Scatterplot

```{r, eval=F}
#requires ggplot2 package
#points with a straight best-fit line
ggplot(DATASET_OBJECT, aes(x = X_VARIABLE, y = Y_VARIABLE)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "black") +
  labs(x = "X_AXIS_LABEL", y = "Y_AXIS_LABEL")
```

### Density Plot

```{r, eval=F}
#requires ggplot2 package
ggplot(DATASET_OBJECT, aes(x = VARIABLE_OF_INTEREST)) +
  geom_density(fill = "lightgrey")
```

### Line Chart

```{r, eval=F}
#requires ggplot2 package
ggplot(DATASET_OBJECT, aes(x = X_VARIABLE, y = Y_VARIABLE)) +
  geom_line()
```

### Cumulative Frequency Plot

```{r, eval=F}
#requires ggplot2 package
ggplot(DATASET_OBJECT, aes(x = VARIABLE_OF_INTEREST)) +
  stat_ecdf()
```

### Adding a Reference Line

```{r, eval=F}
#add a vertical line to any ggplot (for example at the mean)
PLOTCOMMANDS + geom_vline(xintercept = VALUE, linetype = "dashed")

#label every whole number on the x axis
PLOTCOMMANDS + scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:MAX_VALUE)
```

## Maps

```{r, eval = F}
#required tmap package
## classification styles
## "equal"
## "fisher"
## "pretty"
## "quantile"

#command to see color palettes (requires cols4all package)
cols4all::c4a_gui()

##make a basic point map
tm_shape(DATABASE_OBJECT) + tm_dots(fill = "VARIABLE_OF_INTEREST", size = 0.5,
                fill.scale = tm_scale_intervals(values = "brewer.COLOR_PALETTE", style = "CLASSIFICATION", n = NUMBEROFCLASSES))

##make a basic polygon map
tm_shape(DATABASE_OBJECT) + tm_polygons(fill = "VARIABLE_OF_INTEREST",
                fill.scale = tm_scale_intervals(values = "brewer.COLOR_PALETTE", style = "CLASSIFICATION", n = NUMBEROFCLASSES))


## make an interactive map
tmap_mode(mode = "view")

##go back to static map
tmap_mode(mode = "plot")


## add title
MAPCOMMANDS + tm_title("TITLE")


## Add transparency
tm_shape(DATABASE_OBJECT) + tm_polygons(fill = "VARIABLE_OF_INTEREST", fill_alpha = VALUE)

```

### Legends, Colors and Borders

```{r, eval=F}
#give the legend a title
tm_shape(DATABASE_OBJECT) + tm_polygons(fill = "VARIABLE_OF_INTEREST",
                fill.legend = tm_legend(title = "LEGEND_TITLE"))

#reverse a palette by putting a minus sign in front of its name
fill.scale = tm_scale_intervals(values = "-brewer.rd_yl_bu", style = "quantile", n = 5)

#center a diverging palette on zero (for example for residuals)
fill.scale = tm_scale_intervals(values = "brewer.rd_bu", style = "pretty", midpoint = 0)

#hide polygon borders (useful for small polygons like tracts)
tm_shape(DATABASE_OBJECT) + tm_polygons(fill = "VARIABLE_OF_INTEREST", col_alpha = 0)

#choose a color for each category yourself
category_colors <- c("CATEGORY1" = "#B2182B", "CATEGORY2" = "#2166AC")
tm_shape(DATABASE_OBJECT) + tm_polygons(fill = "CATEGORICAL_VARIABLE",
                fill.scale = tm_scale_categorical(values = category_colors))
```

### Checking Class Breaks

```{r, eval=F}
#requires classInt package (installed with tmap)
#the class breaks a classification style makes
breaks <- classInt::classIntervals(na.omit(DATA$VARIABLE), n = 5, style = "quantile")$brks

#how many features fall in each class
table(cut(DATA$VARIABLE, breaks, include.lowest = TRUE))
```

### More Map Types

```{r, eval=F}
#categorical map
tm_shape(DATABASE_OBJECT) + tm_polygons(fill = "CATEGORICAL_VARIABLE",
                fill.scale = tm_scale_categorical(values = "brewer.set2"))

#proportional symbol map (size and optional color)
tm_shape(DATABASE_OBJECT) + tm_symbols(size = "VARIABLE_OF_INTEREST", fill = "VARIABLE_OF_INTEREST")

#raster map
tm_shape(RASTER_OBJECT) + tm_raster(col.scale = tm_scale_intervals(values = "carto.sunset_dark", n = 5))

#outline polygons only
tm_shape(BOUNDARY) + tm_borders()

#bivariate map of two variables
tm_shape(DATABASE_OBJECT) + tm_polygons(fill = tm_vars(c("VARIABLE1", "VARIABLE2"), multivariate = TRUE),
              fill.scale = tm_scale_bivariate(values = "bivario.folk_warmth",
                scale1 = tm_scale_intervals(n = 4, style = "quantile"),
                scale2 = tm_scale_intervals(n = 4, style = "quantile")))

#add a basemap
MAPCOMMANDS + tm_basemap("Esri.WorldGrayCanvas")

#add a legend entry by hand (e.g. for a point you added)
MAPCOMMANDS + tm_add_legend(type = "symbols", labels = "LABEL", fill = "COLOR")

#put two maps side by side
map1 <- tm_shape(DATA1) + tm_polygons(fill = "VARIABLE")
map2 <- tm_shape(DATA2) + tm_polygons(fill = "VARIABLE")
tmap_arrange(map1, map2, ncol = 2)
```

## Descriptive Spatial Statistics

### Mean Center and Weighted Mean Center

```{r, eval = F}
#requires sfdep package

#calculate mean center
DATASET_mean_center <- center_mean(DATASET)

#calculate weighted mean center
DATASET_weighted_center <- center_mean(DATASET, weights = DATASET$VARIABLE)

#distance between two centers (in the units of the CRS; divide feet by 5280 for miles)
st_distance(DATASET_mean_center, DATASET_weighted_center)
```

### Standard Deviational Ellipse

```{r, eval = F}
#requires sfdep package
#std_dev_ellipse() has no weights, so filter to the features you want first
#calculate standard ellipse values
std_ellip_DATASET <- std_dev_ellipse(DATASET)

#create an ellipse of those values
std_ellip_DATASET <- st_ellipse(geometry = std_ellip_DATASET,
                                sx = std_ellip_DATASET$sx,
                                sy = std_ellip_DATASET$sy,
                                rotation = -std_ellip_DATASET$theta)
```

## Probability

### Empirical Probability

```{r, eval = F}
#share of days (rows) where the event happened
p <- mean(DATASET$VARIABLE > VALUE)

#the same thing with a 1/0 column
p <- sum(DATASET$EVENT_COLUMN) / nrow(DATASET)
```

### Binomial Distribution

```{r, eval = F}
#N = number of trials, p = probability of success on each trial
probability_per_outcome <- tibble(
  num_successes = 0:N,
  #here is the main probability function: the probability of exactly x successes
  probability = dbinom(x = 0:N, size = N, prob = p)
)

#most likely number of successes
probability_per_outcome |> slice_max(probability)

#cumulative probability of VALUE or fewer successes
cum_prob <- pbinom(VALUE, size = N, prob = p)

#probability of more than VALUE successes
1 - pbinom(VALUE, size = N, prob = p)

```

### Normal Distribution

```{r, eval = F}
#pnorm calculates the CDF up to the value. Do 1-pnorm to get the probability above that value
prob <- pnorm(VALUEOFINTEREST, mean =  mean(DATASET$VARIABLE), sd = sd(DATASET$VARIABLE))
```

### Plotting a Normal Curve and Checking Normality

```{r, eval=F}
#draw a histogram with the matching normal curve on top
ggplot(DATASET, aes(x = VARIABLE)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), binwidth = BINWIDTH, fill = "lightgrey") +
  stat_function(fun = dnorm, args = list(mean = mean(DATASET$VARIABLE), sd = sd(DATASET$VARIABLE)))

#Q-Q plot: points close to the line mean the data are close to normal
qqnorm(DATASET$VARIABLE)
qqline(DATASET$VARIABLE)
```

## Estimation in Sampling

### Point Estimate and CI for Mean

```{r, eval = F}
#t test command (assumes two-tail)
t.test(DATASET$VARIABLE, conf.level = 0.95)

#the same interval by hand
x_bar <- mean(DATASET$VARIABLE)
s <- sd(DATASET$VARIABLE)
n <- nrow(DATASET)
margin <- qt(0.975, df = n - 1) * s / sqrt(n)
c(x_bar - margin, x_bar + margin)
```

### Point Estimate and CI for Proportion

```{r, eval = F}
prop.test(TOTALSUCCESSES, n, conf.level = 0.95)

#by hand (prop.test adds a small correction, so its interval is slightly different)
p_hat <- TOTALSUCCESSES / n
p_margin <- qnorm(0.975) * sqrt(p_hat * (1 - p_hat) / n)
c(p_hat - p_margin, p_hat + p_margin)
```

### Critical Values

```{r, eval=F}
#z critical value for a 95% confidence level
qnorm(0.975)

#t critical value for a 95% confidence level with n - 1 degrees of freedom
qt(0.975, df = N - 1)
```

### Simulating Repeated Samples

```{r, eval=F}
#take one random sample of size N
one_sample <- sample(DATASET$VARIABLE, size = N, replace = TRUE)

#repeat that many times and keep each sample mean
sample_means <- replicate(NUM_SAMPLES, mean(sample(DATASET$VARIABLE, size = N, replace = TRUE)))

#turn a raster into a table of its cell values (requires terra package)
RASTER_df <- as.data.frame(RASTER)
names(RASTER_df) <- "VARIABLE"
```

## Hypothesis Testing

### One-Sample T-Test

```{r, eval=F}
#remove alternative to run two-sided T-test
t.test(DATASET$VARIABLE, mu = TRUEMEAN, alternative = "less", conf.level = 0.95)
```

### Two-Sample T-Test

```{r, eval=F}
#test for equality of variance (requires car package)
leveneTest(VARIABLE ~ CATEGORY, data = DATASET)

#change var.equal if Levene's test indicates unequal variance
test <- t.test(VARIABLE ~ CATEGORY, data = DATASET, var.equal = TRUE)
test

#the mean of each group
test$estimate

#effect size: the difference between the group means, in the variable's units
diff(test$estimate)
```

### Paired T-Test

```{r, eval=F}
#remove alternative to run two-sided
t.test(DATASET$VARIABLE1, DATASET$VARIABLE2, paired = TRUE, alternative = "greater", conf.level = 0.95)
```

### Chi Square Test of Independence

```{r, eval=F}
counts <- table(DATASET$VARIABLE1, DATASET$VARIABLE2)
chi_test <- chisq.test(counts)
chi_test

#the counts you would expect if the two variables were independent
chi_test$expected
```

## Point Pattern Analysis

### Making a Point Pattern

```{r, eval=F}
#boundary must be owin object (st_union merges polygons like counties into one outline)
boundary_owin <- as.owin(st_union(BOUNDARYOBJECT))

#turn point data into a ppp
data.ppp <- as.ppp(st_geometry(DATA), W = boundary_owin)

#change the units from feet to miles (use 1000, "km" for meters to kilometers)
data.ppp <- rescale(data.ppp, 5280, "mile")

#points at the exact same location break nearest neighbor analysis, so either keep unique locations
data.ppp <- unique(data.ppp)

#or move each point a tiny random distance
data.ppp <- rjitter(data.ppp, radius = SMALL_DISTANCE)
```

### Quadrat Analysis

```{r, eval=F}
#create a quadrat count with 9 quadrats (modify the number of quadrats to fit your case)
q_count <- quadratcount(data.ppp, nx = 3, ny = 3)

#plot the counts on top of the points
plot(data.ppp, pch = 16, cex = 0.5)
plot(q_count, add = TRUE, col = "black")

#variance-to-mean ratio (above 1 suggests clustering, below 1 suggests dispersion)
var(as.vector(q_count)) / mean(as.vector(q_count))

#run quadrat test with monte carlo sims
q_test <- quadrat.test(data.ppp, nx = 3, ny = 3, method = "MonteCarlo", nsim = 999)
```

### Intensity

```{r, eval=F}
#points per unit area (use area.owin, because terra also has an area command)
intensity <- npoints(data.ppp) / area.owin(Window(data.ppp))
```

### Kernel Density

```{r, eval=F}
#estimate KDE
kernel_density <- density(data.ppp)

#map it with the points on top
plot(kernel_density, main = "TITLE")
plot(data.ppp, add = TRUE, pch = 16, cex = 0.5)
```

### ANN Analysis

```{r, eval=F}
#observed and expected (under CSR) average nearest neighbor distance
ANN_obs <- mean(nndist(data.ppp))
ANN_exp <- 0.5 / sqrt(npoints(data.ppp) / area.owin(Window(data.ppp)))

#ANN ratio (below 1 suggests clustering, above 1 suggests dispersion)
ANN_obs / ANN_exp

#Clark-Evans test of the ratio against CSR with monte carlo sims
clarkevans.test(data.ppp, correction = "none", alternative = "two.sided",
                method = "MonteCarlo", nsim = 999)
```

### ANN Against an Inhomogeneous Process

```{r, eval=F}
nsim <- 999
ANN_sim <- numeric(nsim)

#MC simulations
for(i in 1:nsim){
  sim <- rpoispp(kernel_density) #simulate inhomogeneous Poisson using the KDE
  ANN_sim[i] <- mean(nndist(sim))
}

#monte Carlo p-value (two-sided)
N_greater <- sum(ANN_sim >= ANN_obs)
p_value <- 2 * min((N_greater + 1)/(nsim + 1), (nsim - N_greater + 1)/(nsim + 1))

p_value
```

### L-function

```{r, eval=F}
#compare against CSR (homogeneous Poisson). Correction corrects for edge effects.
l_funct_csr <- envelope(
  data.ppp,
  fun = Lest,
  nsim = 99,
  correction = "border",
  transform = expression(. - r)
)
plot(l_funct_csr)

#if the first-order pattern is not uniform, compare against an inhomogeneous Poisson
#simulate from the KDE and give Linhom the same KDE
l_funct_inhom <- envelope(
  data.ppp,
  fun = Linhom,
  nsim = 99,
  simulate = expression(rpoispp(kernel_density)),
  funargs = list(lambda = kernel_density, correction = "border"),
  transform = expression(. - r)
)
plot(l_funct_inhom)
```

## Spatial Autocorrelation and Spatial Modeling

### Calculating Neighbors

```{r, eval=F}
## QUEENS CASE NEIGHBORS ###
#calculate neighbors
nb_queen <- poly2nb(DATASET, queen = TRUE) # queen shares point or border
#set neighborhood weight matrix (zero.policy = TRUE allows features with no neighbors, like islands)
nbw_queen <- nb2listw(nb_queen, style = "W", zero.policy = TRUE)

#see how many neighbors each feature has
summary(nb_queen)

#draw the neighbor links
plot(st_geometry(DATASET), border = "grey")
plot(nb_queen, st_coordinates(st_centroid(st_geometry(DATASET))), add = TRUE)


## DISTANCE BASED NEIGHBORS ##
#needs points (use st_centroid() first for polygons), threshold is units in CRS
nb_dist <- dnearneigh(DATASET, d1 = 0, d2 = THRESHOLD)
#set neighborhood weight matrix
nbw_dist <- nb2listw(nb_dist, style = "W", zero.policy = TRUE)


## K NEAREST NEIGHBORS ####
#needs points (use st_centroid() first for polygons), k = number of neighbors
knn <- knearneigh(DATASET, k = NUMNEIGHBORS)
#calculate neighborhoods
nb_knn  <- knn2nb(knn)
#set neighborhood weight matrix
nbw_knn <- nb2listw(nb_knn, style = "W")

```

### Global Moran's I

```{r, eval=F}
gmoran <- moran.test(DATASET$VARIABLE, NBWMATRIX)
```

### Moran's I with a Permutation Test

```{r, eval=F}
#Monte Carlo test of global Moran's I
set.seed(391)
gmoran <- moran.mc(DATA$VARIABLE, NBWMATRIX, nsim = 999)
gmoran

#Moran scatterplot of each value against its neighbors' average
moran.plot(DATA$VARIABLE, NBWMATRIX, xlab = "X_AXIS_LABEL", ylab = "Y_AXIS_LABEL")
```

### LISA

```{r, eval=F}
#local Moran's I with a permutation test for each feature
set.seed(391)
locali <- localmoran_perm(DATASET$VARIABLE, NBWMATRIX, nsim = 999)
head(locali)

#add the p-value and the quadrant, and label features that are not significant
DATASET <- DATASET |>
  mutate(lisa_p = locali[, "Pr(z != E(Ii)) Sim"],
         lisa_quad = as.character(attr(locali, "quadr")$mean),
         lisa_cluster = ifelse(lisa_p < 0.05, lisa_quad, "Not significant"))

#how many features are in each cluster type
table(DATASET$lisa_cluster)

#map the clusters
lisa_colors <- c("High-High" = "#B2182B", "Low-Low" = "#2166AC", "High-Low" = "#F4A582",
                 "Low-High" = "#92C5DE", "Not significant" = "#E5E5E5")
tm_shape(DATASET) +
  tm_polygons(fill = "lisa_cluster",
              fill.scale = tm_scale_categorical(values = lisa_colors),
              fill.legend = tm_legend(title = "LISA cluster"))
```

### Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) Regression

```{r, eval=F}
#fit a linear regression
fit.ols <- lm(DEPENDENT ~ INDEPENDENT + INDEPENDENT, data = DATA)

#see results
summary(fit.ols)

#save the residuals to map them or test them for autocorrelation
DATA <- DATA |> mutate(residuals = resid(fit.ols))
```

### Testing Residuals for Spatial Autocorrelation

```{r, eval=F}
#Moran's I of the OLS residuals
lm.morantest(fit.ols, nbw)

#Lagrange multiplier tests to choose between a lag and an error model (requires spdep 1.3-1 or newer)
lm.RStests(fit.ols, nbw, test = c("RSerr", "RSlag", "adjRSerr", "adjRSlag"))
```

### Traditional Spatial Models

```{r, eval=F}
#requires spatialreg package
#lag model
fit.lag <- lagsarlm(DEPENDENT ~ INDEPENDENT + INDEPENDENT,
                  data = DATA,
                  listw = nbw)
#see results
summary(fit.lag)

#error model
fit.error <- errorsarlm(DEPENDENT ~ INDEPENDENT + INDEPENDENT,
                  data = DATA,
                  listw = nbw)
#see results
summary(fit.error)

#compare models (lower AIC is better)
AIC(fit.ols, fit.lag, fit.error)

#check whether the spatial model removed the autocorrelation in the residuals
moran.test(residuals(fit.error), nbw)
```

### Geographically Weighted Regression (GWR)

```{r, eval=F}
#requires GWmodel package
#data must be projected and have no missing values in the model variables
#choose the bandwidth (adaptive = TRUE means the bandwidth is a number of neighbors)
bw <- bw.gwr(DEPENDENT ~ INDEPENDENT + INDEPENDENT, data = DATA,
             approach = "AICc", kernel = "bisquare", adaptive = TRUE)

#fit the GWR
fit.gwr <- gwr.basic(DEPENDENT ~ INDEPENDENT + INDEPENDENT, data = DATA,
                     bw = bw, kernel = "bisquare", adaptive = TRUE)

#see results (global and local coefficients)
fit.gwr

#the local results as an sf object you can map with tmap
gwr_results <- st_as_sf(fit.gwr$SDF)

#each predictor's local coefficient is a column with the predictor's name, local R2 is Local_R2
tm_shape(gwr_results) + tm_polygons(fill = "INDEPENDENT")
tm_shape(gwr_results) + tm_polygons(fill = "Local_R2")
```

### K-Means Clustering

```{r, eval=F}
#keep the variables to cluster on and standardize them (mean 0, sd 1)
cluster_vars <- DATA |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  select(VARIABLE1, VARIABLE2, VARIABLE3, VARIABLE4) |>
  scale()

#elbow plot: total within-cluster sum of squares for 1 to 10 clusters
set.seed(391)
wss <- sapply(1:10, function(k) kmeans(cluster_vars, centers = k, nstart = 25)$tot.withinss)
ggplot(data.frame(k = 1:10, wss = wss), aes(x = k, y = wss)) +
  geom_line() + geom_point() +
  labs(x = "Number of clusters", y = "Total within-cluster sum of squares")

#run k-means with the number of clusters you chose
set.seed(391)
km <- kmeans(cluster_vars, centers = NUM_CLUSTERS, nstart = 25)

#add the cluster to the data (as a category, so it maps with categorical colors)
DATA <- DATA |> mutate(cluster = as.character(km$cluster))

#average of each variable in each cluster, to name the clusters
DATA |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  group_by(cluster) |>
  summarise(across(c(VARIABLE1, VARIABLE2, VARIABLE3, VARIABLE4), mean), n = n())
```

## Continuous Surfaces

### Setting Up for Interpolation

```{r, eval=F}
#requires gstat and terra packages
#points must be projected. Make a table of coordinates and values
DATA_df <- data.frame(x = st_coordinates(DATA)[, 1],
                      y = st_coordinates(DATA)[, 2],
                      value = DATA$VARIABLE)

#empty raster covering the boundary (resolution is the cell size in the units of the CRS)
grid <- rast(vect(BOUNDARY), resolution = CELL_SIZE)
```

### IDW

```{r, eval=F}
#set up the IDW model (idp is the power)
idw_model <- gstat(formula = value ~ 1, locations = ~x + y, data = DATA_df,
                   set = list(idp = 2))

#predict a value for every raster cell
idw_surface <- interpolate(grid, idw_model, debug.level = 0)

#mask to boundaries
idw_surface <- mask(idw_surface, vect(BOUNDARY))

#map the predictions
tm_shape(idw_surface[["var1.pred"]]) +
  tm_raster(col.scale = tm_scale_intervals(style = "quantile", n = 5, values = "-brewer.rd_yl_bu"))
```

### Cross-Validation

```{r, eval=F}
#leave-one-out cross-validation of IDW
cv <- krige.cv(value ~ 1, locations = ~x + y, data = DATA_df,
               set = list(idp = 2), verbose = FALSE)

#leave-one-out cross-validation of kriging
cv <- krige.cv(value ~ 1, locations = ~x + y, data = DATA_df,
               model = vgm_fit, verbose = FALSE)

#root mean squared error
sqrt(mean(cv$residual^2))
```

### Kriging

```{r, eval=F}
#compute empirical variogram
v <- variogram(value ~ 1, locations = ~x + y, data = DATA_df)

#plot empirical variogram
plot(v)

#see the shapes of the available variogram models
show.vgms()

#fit a variogram model ("Sph", "Exp" or "Gau"); give several and R picks the best fit
vgm_fit <- fit.variogram(v, vgm("Sph"))
vgm_fit

#or give starting values yourself
vgm_fit <- fit.variogram(v, vgm(psill = FILL, model = "FILL", range = FILL, nugget = FILL))

#plot fitted variogram model
plot(v, vgm_fit)

#fit kriging
krige_model <- gstat(formula = value ~ 1, locations = ~x + y, data = DATA_df,
                     model = vgm_fit)
krige_surface <- interpolate(grid, krige_model, debug.level = 0)

#mask to boundary
krige_surface <- mask(krige_surface, vect(BOUNDARY))

#predictions are in var1.pred and the kriging variance is in var1.var
tm_shape(krige_surface[["var1.pred"]]) + tm_raster()
tm_shape(krige_surface[["var1.var"]]) + tm_raster()

```

### Summarizing a Surface by Polygon

```{r, eval=F}
#average predicted value in each polygon (for example each county)
#the polygons must be in the same CRS as the raster
polygon_means <- terra::extract(SURFACE[["var1.pred"]], vect(POLYGONS), fun = mean, na.rm = TRUE)

#add the averages to the polygons (rows come back in the same order)
POLYGONS <- POLYGONS |> mutate(mean_pred = polygon_means$var1.pred)
```
